page: Amazon Web Services t2.2xlarge is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine hosted on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz, configured with 8 vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 45 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB DDR RAM, delivering a 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The instance includes no bundled local storage, relying on external network volumes, and provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate multi-threaded capacity paired with lower single-thread and memory write figures. The instance achieves middle-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (11,556.72) and Geekbench multi-core evaluation (4,812.0). Conversely, single-core processing registers in the bottom decile, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 874.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression of 7.12 GB/sec. Large block memory write bandwidth measures 24.83 GB/sec. Database operations score 5,634.84 in PassMark tests, whereas Redis SET operations reach 0.87 million operations per second and static web serving delivers 1.95 GB/sec.

The burstable credit structure offers resource density and cost efficiency for workloads that experience intermittent utilization rather than persistent full-core load. A continuous compute draw will exhaust credit balances, resulting in baseline performance throttles. Given the 8-vCPU and 32 GB configuration, the t2.2xlarge fits development environments, staging systems, code compilation tasks, batch jobs, and general-purpose business applications with variable traffic patterns.
description: Amazon Web Services t2.2xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance configured with 8 vCPUs on an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor at 2.3 GHz. Running on the Xen hypervisor, it features 32.0 GB of system memory, a 1 Gbps baseline network allocation, and no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate average multi-core throughput, including 11,556.72 in stress-ng multi-core and 4,812.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, alongside steady PassMark compilation and database marks. Single-core performance and uncached memory writes place in lower benchmark tiers, with Geekbench single-core scoring 874.0 and memory write bandwidth reaching 24.83 GB/sec. Utilizing a burstable CPU credit architecture, the instance provides cost efficiency for non-continuous compute demands, fitting code compilation, staging environments, batch processing, and variable-load enterprise applications.
